description: Returns the 2026 or 2027 standard deduction piece by piece — the basic amount, the additional amount for 65 or older and blind, a dependent's limit, the married-filing-separately rule — free; and, with a connected QuantCalc PRO licence or Tax Season Pass, the senior deduction after its phase-out, the itemized total (SALT cap, mortgage interest, charity and medical floors, the IRC 68 limit), the non-itemizer charitable deduction, the federal tax both ways and which is lower, from QuantCalc's federal tax API run twice. The amounts are the website's standard deduction pages' own figures (2027 projected until the IRS publishes them). Not tax advice.

age.description: Your age on December 31 of the tax year (0-120): 65 or older adds the additional amount and the senior deduction.

dependent.description: Not on a joint return: someone else can claim you as a dependent (the basic amount is limited, IRC 63(c)(5)). Default false.

filing_status.description: 2026 filing status: single, married filing jointly (mfj), married filing separately (mfs) or head of household (hoh).

retirement_income.description: Taxable pension, annuity and IRA income. Default 0.

spouse_age.description: Joint return only: the spouse's age. Default: the same as age.

spouse_blind.description: Joint return only: the spouse is blind. Default false.

spouse_itemizes.description: mfs only: your spouse itemizes on a separate return, so you must too.

spouse_wages.description: Joint return only: the spouse's wages. Default 0.

state_local_income_tax_paid.description: State and local income tax paid. Default 0.

tax_year.description: 2026 (default) or 2027. 2027 uses the 2027 pages' figures (projected until the IRS publishes them) and the engine's projected federal return; stated in the result.

wages.description: Your wages (a dependent's earned income). Default 0.

name: standard_deduction_vs_itemizing
title: Standard deduction piece by piece, and whether itemizing beats it (2026, 2027 projected)
